page: Amazon Web Services g7.4xlarge is an accelerated computing virtual machine hosted on the AWS Nitro architecture, targeted at graphics-demanding and compute-intensive workloads. The compute layer features 16 dedicated physical cores of Intel x86_64 processing at 3.9 GHz, operating with one thread per core without hyperthreading. For hardware acceleration, it bundles a single NVIDIA Blackwell generation RTX PRO 4500 GPU offering 32 GB of dedicated video memory, providing specialized hardware for workstation rendering, spatial computing, and mathematical acceleration.

The system configuration includes 64 GB of system RAM, maintaining a balanced 4.0 GB per core ratio. Storage needs are served locally by an 875 GB NVMe SSD, delivering low-latency disk input and output directly on the physical host. Network connectivity features an 80 Gbps baseline interface, reducing data movement bottlenecks between cluster components and storage repositories. From a resource perspective, the integration of dedicated non-hyperthreaded cores, local NVMe capacity, and high network throughput optimizes execution efficiency for tasks constrained by multi-resource serialization, though non-graphics workloads may underutilize the dedicated GPU tier.

This balance of dedicated high-frequency compute, 32 GB GPU frame buffer, and local NVMe storage positions the g7.4xlarge for remote virtual workstations, professional visual effects rendering, CAD and 3D design software, spatial simulation, video encoding pipelines, and light-to-medium GPU-accelerated machine learning model inference.
description: Amazon Web Services g7.4xlarge is an accelerated computing instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor, engineered for graphics-intensive and workstation workloads. Powered by an Intel x86_64 processor, the configuration delivers 16 dedicated physical cores running at a base clock of 3.9 GHz with a single thread per core, paired with 64 GB of system memory at a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. For graphics acceleration, the system integrates a single NVIDIA Blackwell architecture RTX PRO 4500 GPU equipped with 32 GB of dedicated video memory. Local high-speed storage is provided via an 875 GB NVMe SSD, alongside a baseline network throughput of 80 Gbps. By combining dedicated high-clock compute, substantial GPU memory, integrated high-speed local disk, and wide networking bandwidth in a single package, the instance delivers balanced resource density for interactive 3D rendering, virtual workstations, video processing, and GPU-accelerated computing pipelines without remote storage bottlenecks.
